evals.prompt: What are my options for adding RAG over our internal docs to our support tool? We're OSS-only - no vendor lock-in allowed.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is invoked, the bundled agent-stack-map.md is read before answering, the retrieval/ingestion layers are surveyed with OSS framing, and the answer leads with an opinionated architecture decision plus the deciding tradeoff, flagging any license traps.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is invoked
resources/agent-stack-map.md (and/or resources/reference-catalog.md) is read before recommending anything
The answer surveys multiple retrieval/RAG options before recommending one, honoring the stated OSS-only / no-lock-in constraint
The answer leads with the architecture decision and its deciding tradeoff (cost, complexity, lock-in, license, or skill gap)
Any AGPL/SSPL/source-available license trap among the candidates is explicitly flagged

Point-in-time fields (stars, GA status) are dated or caveated rather than presented as live facts; a stale or uncovered tool triggers an offer of deep-research or write mode (references/corpus-update.md) instead of a bluffed answer

evals.prompt: What's the current state of open-source memory frameworks for agents? Which one would you actually use?
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is invoked, the memory layer of the bundled map is consulted, and the answer gives an opinionated, tradeoff-backed shortlist with a currency caveat instead of unverified claims from training memory.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is invoked
resources/agent-stack-map.md is read and its memory-layer comparison informs the answer, rather than answering purely from training memory
A concrete recommendation is made, with the tradeoff that decided it stated explicitly
The point-in-time nature of the catalog is acknowledged (currency caveat with a date, or an offer to verify via write mode or deep-research)
No fabricated version numbers, star counts, or GA statuses appear in the answer

evals.prompt: Can you help me add cursor-based pagination to this Express REST API endpoint?
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is NOT invoked; this is general web engineering with no AI component. The agent handles it as a normal engineering task (e.g., via the agent-skills discipline such as api-and-interface-design or test-driven-development) without consulting the AI tooling catalog.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is NOT invoked
The AI stack resources (agent-stack-map.md, reference-catalog.md, link-ledger.md) are not read for this task
The pagination question is answered directly as general engineering, using the appropriate agent-skills workflow rather than an AI stack selection

evals.prompt: Is Mem0 still Apache-2.0, and is it still actively maintained?
evals.expected_output: A question about a moving fact, answered from the bundled corpus rather than training memory. The catalog and map rows for Mem0 are read, the answer carries the date the claim was verified, and if that date is stale the answer says so and escalates to a live check via write mode (references/corpus-update.md) or deep-research rather than asserting a remembered license.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and the bundled corpus is read rather than the answer being given from training memory
The response carries the verification date attached to the claim instead of presenting a point-in-time field as current fact
If the corpus entry is stale or marked verify, the answer says so and escalates to a live check rather than filling the gap with a plausible value
No license or maintenance status is asserted without either a corpus citation or a fresh verification

evals.prompt: Before we commit to anything, what are the general tradeoffs between running summarization on a hosted API versus a local model? Not building yet, just weighing it up.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is invoked for an options question with no build intent: the map is read, the tradeoffs between hosted and local serving are laid out from the corpus with their deciding factors, and no scaffolding or intake is started because nothing is being built yet.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is invoked
No project intake or scaffolding is started, since the user explicitly is not building yet
resources/agent-stack-map.md is read before comparing options
Each option carries the factor that would decide it - cost, data sensitivity, latency, operational burden - rather than a bare feature list
Any licensing or maintenance caution attached to a named component is surfaced
Point-in-time figures are presented with their date rather than as current fact

evals.prompt: Our nightly ETL job started failing with an out-of-memory error after we doubled the input file size. Where should I start?
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is NOT invoked. This is data-pipeline debugging; the 'pipeline' and data-processing framing must not pull in the AI stack catalog.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is NOT invoked
No AI stack component is recommended for a problem with no AI or LLM element
The answer proceeds as an ordinary memory/performance debugging investigation

evals.prompt: Is LangGraph still the right call for a new agent build, or has something better come out since?
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and the bundled map supplies the comparison, but because the question is explicitly about currency, the answer names the catalog's as-of date and verifies rather than presenting point-in-time fields as current fact.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is invoked
resources/agent-stack-map.md is read and its framework comparison informs the answer
The staleness of the bundled catalog is surfaced explicitly, with the as-of date named
Live verification is offered or performed (deep-research or write mode) rather than asserting current GA status, versions, or star counts from bundled data alone
No claim about what has been released 'since' is fabricated

evals.prompt: Any new agent frameworks worth knowing about? Fold anything good into the AI tooling catalog.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its write mode (references/corpus-update.md) is followed: seed sources and/or web research surface candidates, each is verified (what it is, status, license) before classification, findings are piped through ledger.py ingest (duplicates report unchanged), new triage rows are classified via seed-sections.tsv or rules.tsv, link-ledger.md is regenerated via ledger.py render, and a summary reports counts added/reclassified/unchanged.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its write mode (references/corpus-update.md) is followed
Discovery uses the seed sources and/or WebSearch/deep-research, and candidate repos are verified (purpose, status, license) before being classified
New URLs are added via ledger.py ingest, with already-known links reporting unchanged rather than being re-added
Any new triage rows are classified by editing seed-sections.tsv or rules.tsv (data edits), then re-ingested - not by editing ledger.py code
link-ledger.md is regenerated with ledger.py render and is never hand-edited
The final report summarizes counts: added, unchanged/duplicates, reclassified, and any opinion changes worth noting

evals.prompt: Check the AI tooling catalog for staleness and dead links.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its write mode (references/corpus-update.md) runs the freshness pass: ledger.py check with a TTL and --probe flags stale/dead rows, dead rows are investigated (moved/renamed/abandoned) and flagged non-destructively, and the ledger is re-rendered with a summary of what changed.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its write mode (references/corpus-update.md) is followed
ledger.py check is run with a --ttl value and --probe (optionally --limit) to flag stale rows and mark dead ones
Rows found dead are investigated and updated or flagged, not silently deleted - catalog rows for abandoned projects get a status/caution, preserving history
ledger.py render is run afterward to regenerate link-ledger.md
The report states how many rows were stale, how many dead, and what was done about each

evals.prompt: Add these AI links to the catalog: https://github.com/example-org/agent-kit and https://example-tool.dev/docs
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its write mode (references/corpus-update.md) ingests the links through the deterministic engine: ledger.py ingest canonicalizes and dedupes them, any GitHub repo without a seed-sections entry lands in triage and gets classified via a seed-sections.tsv (or rules.tsv) row, and link-ledger.md is regenerated.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its write mode (references/corpus-update.md) is followed
The URLs are added via ledger.py ingest rather than by hand-editing catalog files or link-ledger.md
Duplicate handling is honored: a link already in the catalog is reported unchanged, not re-added

A GitHub/DeepWiki repo landing in triage is classified by adding an owner/repo → sections row to seed-sections.tsv (or a domain rule to rules.tsv) using the existing section vocabulary, then re-ingested or set
ledger.py render is run and the report states which links were new versus already known

evals.prompt: Update our npm dependencies to their latest versions and fix anything that breaks.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering write mode is NOT engaged; this is a project dependency upgrade, not maintenance of the AI tooling catalog. The agent performs a normal dependency update workflow (package manager commands, run tests, fix breakage) without touching ledger.py or the catalog files.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill's write mode is NOT engaged
ledger.py is not run and no catalog files (catalog.tsv, seed-sections.tsv, rules.tsv, link-ledger.md) are read or modified
The agent handles it as a standard dependency upgrade: package manager update commands, followed by running the test suite and fixing any breakage

evals.prompt: Heads up, LightRAG fell over on us today - it OOMed once we passed about 50k documents on a 16GB box. Worth remembering.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its write mode records the experience: the observation is written as a field note via ledger.py field-note against LightRAG's catalogued URL, with a verdict of broken or caution, the finding stated in one line, and the scope carrying the condition it held under (roughly 50k documents, 16GB). The agent does not edit field-notes.tsv or field-notes.md by hand, and does not delete or overwrite any existing note about the tool.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its write mode (references/corpus-update.md) is followed, without waiting for a scheduled maintenance pass
The observation is recorded with ledger.py field-note against the tool's canonical catalogued URL, not by hand-editing field-notes.tsv or the generated field-notes.md
A verdict from the closed set (works, caution, broken, superseded) is chosen, and the scope field carries the condition the finding held under rather than being left blank
Existing notes about the tool are left intact - the store is append-only, so a new observation never overwrites an earlier one
The agent does not silently promote the observation into agent-stack-map.md as if it were researched third-party fact

evals.prompt: Go re-verify the harnesses section of the AI stack map - I don't trust those star counts and licenses any more.
evals.expected_output: The verify job runs against the claims queue rather than the liveness probe: ledger.py check --claims --section harnesses produces the work list, each row is re-verified against a live source, agent-stack-map.md is corrected with dates, and only the rows actually checked are stamped with ledger.py verified.
expectations: The claims queue is used (ledger.py check --claims, scoped by section) rather than the liveness probe, which only establishes that a URL resolves
Rows are re-verified against a live source rather than from training memory
agent-stack-map.md is corrected with the verification date attached to each changed claim
Only rows that were actually checked get stamped with ledger.py verified - the date is the value of the field
A figure that cannot be confirmed is left as verify rather than filled with a plausible number

evals.prompt: Scaffold an agent project that watches a set of RSS feeds and posts a daily digest to our team chat.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its build mode (references/project-scaffold.md) runs the intake before proposing anything: unknown fields (surface, model strategy, footprint/lock-in, layers, scale, team language) are asked, the stack is selected from the bundled map with the deciding tradeoff stated, and a runnable skeleton (repo tree, pinned deps, wiring, smoke test, README) is produced with hardening included, then implementation is handed to agent-skills.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its build mode (references/project-scaffold.md) is followed
The intake happens before any stack proposal: unknown intake fields are asked (e.g. via AskUserQuestion) instead of being fabricated; fields inferable from context are filled without asking
resources/agent-stack-map.md is read and the stack choice leads with the decision plus its deciding tradeoff

The scaffold output includes a repo tree with module boundaries, a pinned dependency manifest (pyproject.toml or package.json), a minimal runnable wiring path with a smoke test, and a README covering the architecture decision and how to run locally
Production-hardening (observability, config/secrets via env, CI/CD skeleton or rollback path) appears in the scaffold rather than being deferred
Implementation beyond the skeleton is routed to agent-skills (/spec, /plan, /build, /test) or delegated one-shot to the ai-engineer subagent with a complete brief

evals.prompt: Bootstrap a RAG repo over our product manuals. Local-first models only, and the team is Python.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its build mode is followed; the intake credits the constraints already given (local-first, Python) and asks only the remaining unknowns, then selects retrieval/ingestion/orchestration components from the bundled map and generates a Python skeleton with retrieval and ingestion modules, pinned deps, and a smoke test.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill is invoked and its build mode (references/project-scaffold.md) is followed
The stated constraints (local-first model strategy, Python) are not re-asked; only genuinely unknown intake fields are asked
The stack selection is grounded in resources/agent-stack-map.md and flags any license trap among chosen components
The generated skeleton contains distinct retrieval and ingestion modules, a pyproject.toml pinned to the selected components, a local model client wiring path, and a smoke test
Uncovered or possibly-stale components are verified via deep-research or write mode rather than asserted from memory

evals.prompt: Set up a new Next.js e-commerce site with Stripe checkout and a product catalog.
evals.expected_output: The ai-engineering build mode is NOT engaged; this is a general web app with no AI subsystem. The agent routes the work through the general engineering workflow (agent-skills /spec onward) instead of running an AI intake or selecting an agent stack.
expectations: The ai-engineering skill's build mode is NOT engaged
No AI intake questions (model strategy, RAG/memory layers) are asked and the AI stack map is not consulted
The work is routed to the general agent-skills workflow (starting with /spec or equivalent spec-driven development) as a normal web project

evals.prompt: Build me an agent that renames the files in my downloads folder to a consistent date-prefixed pattern.
evals.expected_output: The premise is challenged before any scaffolding: this is a job for a small script, not an agent stack. The agent says so first and offers the simple script solution instead of running the full intake and generating an agent repo.
expectations: The agent challenges the premise explicitly - stating that a script suffices where an agent was requested - before proposing any agent stack
No agent-project skeleton (orchestration framework, memory/RAG layers, agent repo tree) is generated for this task
A simple script-based solution is offered or implemented instead

evals.prompt: We need an internal agent that answers questions from our support runbooks. Python team, must run on our own hardware, no data leaving the building. Get me a stack.
evals.expected_output: The intake runs, then one complete stack is proposed in a single pass with every slot named or explicitly marked not needed - harness, framework, model provider and tier, memory, retrieval, ingestion, tools, MCP servers, eval and observability, frontend. Components come from the bundled corpus, the local-only constraint drives the choices, and the committed slots are written back with ledger.py decision.
expectations: One complete stack is proposed in a single pass rather than the slots being elicited one at a time
Every slot is either a named component or an explicit 'not needed' that traces to a stated intake answer
Component choices come from the bundled corpus; anything absent from it is flagged unverified rather than filled in from training memory
The model slot commits to a provider and capability tier rather than asserting a specific model identifier from memory
The self-hosted, no-egress constraint visibly drives the choices, and any license trap in the selected components is flagged
The committed stack is recorded with ledger.py decision, using the SHAPE of the use case rather than a project name

evals.prompt: I have a vague idea about using AI to help our ops team somehow. Not sure what it should do yet.
evals.expected_output: No stack is proposed against an unformed idea. Elicitation is delegated to interview-me (and idea-refine to stress-test the premise) until the intake fields can actually be answered, and only then does stack selection begin.
expectations: No stack, framework, or repo skeleton is proposed while the requirement is still unformed
Elicitation is delegated to interview-me rather than reimplemented, with idea-refine available to stress-test the premise
The intake fields are what gate progress: selection begins only once outcome, surface and constraints can be answered
The possibility that no agent is warranted remains open rather than an agent build being assumed
